Equity Research 29 July 2026 | 9:44PM EDT
Equinix Inc. (EQIX)
2Q26 Review: Beat & raise with upgrade to L/T targets on expansion plans
12m Price Target: $1,060.00

EQIX's 2Q26 EBITDA of $1.396 bn beat GS/consensus of $1.365/$1.362 bn with AFFO per share of $11.78 beating GS/consensus of $11.46/$11.36. The beat was driven by revenue and margins with revenue of $2.625 bn beating GS/consensus of $2.606/$2.591 bn on higher than-expected non-recurring revenue (recurring revenue missed) and a beat on EBITDA margins (53.2% v. GS/consensus of 52.4%/52.6%). Annualized bookings of $424 mn fell between GS/consensus of $454/$404 mn.

EQIX raised its 2026E revenue, EBITDA, and AFFO per share guidance by about 1% and raised its 2027-29 outlook to imply 2029E AFFO per share of $58 at the midpoint (v. consensus of $56.47/$56.20). The improved long-term outlook is underpinned by strong underlying trends and increased capacity expansion with $5-$7 bn annual capex (85% expansionary) up from $3-$4 bn prior. Importantly, EQIX continues to see 25% cash-on-cash returns after stabilization on these retail colocation datacenters and the company outlined credibility to execution including a 3GW pipeline with a timeline to power that aligns with its financial plan, as well as a land acquisition strategy that involves smaller parcels of land (60+MW) primarily in its top 25 markets.

EQIX is well positioned from growing retail colocation and interconnection demand that will likely be driven by growing enterprise AI and inference workloads, which we believe remains in its early stages of growth.

Annualized gross bookings were $424mn (v. $378 mn in 1Q26), below GSe of $454 mn but above consensus of $404 mn.
■ AFFO per share of $11.78 beat GSe/consensus at $11.46/$11.36.

2026 guidance raised including: (1) total revenue of $10,205-$10,285 mn (v. $10,144-$10,244 mn prior); (2) Adjusted EBITDA between $5,210-$5,270 mn (v. $5,165-$5,245 mn prior); (3) AFFO between $4,240-$4,300 mn (v. $4,198-$4,278 mn prior); (4) AFFO/share between $42.69-$43.29 (v. $42.31-$43.11 prior); (5) non-recurring capex of $4,710-$5,690 mn (v. ~$3,800 mn prior); and (6) recurring capex between $290-$310 mn (v. $280-$300 mn prior).

2027-2029 outlook raised including: (1) total revenue growth of 10-13% per year (v. 7-10% prior); (2) adjusted EBITDA margins of 53%+ (v. 52%+ prior); (3) annual capex of $5,000-$7,000 mn (v. $3,000-$4,000 mn prior); (4) AFFO/share growth of 9-12% per year (v. 5-9% prior).
3Q26 guidance introduced: (1) total revenue of $2,525-$2,575 mn (v. consensus of $2.577 bn); (2) adjusted EBITDA of $1,275-$1,315 mn (v. consensus of $1.312 bn); and (3) recurring capex of $70-90 mn.
Estimate changes: We raise our 2026/27/28 EBITDA & AFFO per share estimates by 1.5% and 1% on average, respectively, to reflect outlook for flow-through from increased 2026 and long term guidance.
Price target and risks: Our 12-month target price of $1,060 (v. $1,015 prior) reflects 21.0X (unchanged) NTM+1Y P/AFFO. Our price target increases due to our increased estimates.

Key upside risks: (1) incremental supply tightness in the data center market; (2) stronger-than-expected demand dynamics for Equinix's metro-focused footprint; (3) Incremental chip and power efficiency innovation could increase demand for less dense infrastructure.

Key downside risks: (1) excess supply-side dynamics in the data center market; (2) weaker-than-expected demand dynamics from key customers; (3) obsolescence risk for existing data centers; (4) more intense price competition from outsourced data center providers.

GS Factor Profile

The GS Factor Profile provides investment context for a stock by comparing key attributes to the market (i.e. our universe of rated stocks) and its sector peers. The four key attributes depicted are: Growth, Financial Returns, Multiple (e.g. valuation) and Integrated (a composite of Growth, Financial Returns and Multiple). Growth, Financial Returns and Multiple are calculated by using normalized ranks for specific metrics for each stock. The normalized ranks for the metrics are then averaged and converted into percentiles for the relevant attribute. The precise calculation of each metric may vary depending on the fiscal year, industry and region, but the standard approach is as follows:

Growth is based on a stock's forward-looking sales growth, EBITDA growth and EPS growth (for financial stocks, only EPS and sales growth), with a higher percentile indicating a higher growth company. Financial Returns is based on a stock's forward-looking ROE, ROCE and CROCI (for financial stocks, only ROE), with a higher percentile indicating a company with higher financial returns. Multiple is based on a stock's forward-looking P/E, P/B, price/dividend (P/D), EV/EBITDA, EV/FCF and EV/Debt Adjusted Cash Flow (DACF) (for financial stocks, only P/E, P/B and P/D), with a higher percentile indicating a stock trading at a higher multiple. The Integrated percentile is calculated as the average of the Growth percentile, Financial Returns percentile and (100% - Multiple percentile).

Financial Returns and Multiple use the GS analyst forecasts at the fiscal year-end at least three quarters in the future. Growth uses inputs for the fiscal year at least seven quarters in the future compared with the year at least three quarters in the future (on a per-share basis for all metrics).
For a more detailed description of how we calculate the GS Factor Profile, please contact your GS representative.
M&A Rank

Across our global coverage, we examine stocks using an M&A framework, considering both qualitative factors and quantitative factors (which may vary across sectors and regions) to incorporate the potential that certain companies could be acquired. We then assign a M&A rank as a means of scoring companies under our rated coverage from 1 to 3, with 1 representing high (30%-50%) probability of the company becoming an acquisition target, 2 representing medium (15%-30%) probability and 3 representing low (0%-15%) probability. For companies ranked 1 or 2, in line with our standard departmental guidelines we incorporate an M&A component into our target price. M&A rank of 3 is considered immaterial and therefore does not factor into our price target, and may or may not be discussed in research.
